What was the critical error I made that made me instantly fail my driving test?
I am trying to earn my driver's licence in CA but my test was cut short because of the critical speed error of "drove 15mph in a 25mph area for one block. there were no children or objects on road".  
During the test, I saw a 25mph sign, then a school zone sign 2-3 blocks later(the school zone sign did not have a speed limit sign below it). I slowed to 15 to err on the side of caution but the examiner told me to speed up and I had already failed my test. Was I wrong to slow down? Did the 25mph limit hold in the school zone as well?  
I haven't a clue how to interpret this. Am I supposed to know for a fact that children aren't present nearby while I am going 25? I would really appreciate if someone who drives could explain this to me. Thanks!
